transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you, and thank you so much for seeing me today. 

Um... I guess I'm here because I've been feeling like I'm just always running hot? Like I can't ever really shut the motor off, if that makes sense. Which, you know, is usually a good thing—I'm a firefighter, so being ready to go and having high energy is actually a big plus, right? 

But... well, lately it's been getting me into a little bit of trouble at the firehouse. Nothing too crazy, just some friction with the guys and the captain. I hope I'm explaining that okay... is that the kind of information you're looking for?
Have these periods of high energy and feeling like you can't shut your motor off been present for most of your life, or do they come and go in distinct episodes?

Well, um... I think it's pretty much been my whole life, honestly. It doesn't really come and go in episodes. 

My mom actually says I was just like this back in grade school, too. You know, just a really enthusiastic, active kid! I guess I had a bit of a habit of being out of my seat a lot, or maybe blurting out answers a little too eagerly. And, well... I'd lose my homework sometimes, or get notes sent home to my parents. But I was always bright enough to do the work! It was just a little typical energetic boy stuff, I think? Nothing too terrible. 

I hope that's not too bad... does that answer what you were asking?
Do you find that you currently struggle to stay focused on tasks or keep track of your belongings at work or home?

Um, well... I guess I do have a little trouble with focus sometimes, but it's not like I'm totally checked out or anything! 

Like, at work, we have these briefings, or sometimes we do drone training. And I'm always really locked in for the first few minutes, you know? I want to do a good job. But then... well, sometimes I'll suddenly realize I've just been staring at the map or the screen, and I kind of missed half of what command just said. 

It's just that my mind wanders a bit, I think? I always try to catch up, though! I don't want to seem like I don't care, because I really do. Is it normal to zone out a little bit during those long meetings? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad firefighter...
Do you find yourself frequently interrupting others while they are speaking or acting without thinking through the consequences?

Um... well, I guess I do sometimes jump in a little early? But it's really just because I'm so engaged, you know? 

Like, when the guys are talking through a plan at the station, sometimes the answer just pops into my head so fast, and I get really excited to help out. So I might... cut in before they're totally finished? And then I realize I kind of stepped on somebody's toes or messed up the flow of the discussion. 

I never mean anything bad by it, I promise! I just want to contribute and get things moving. I try really hard to catch myself when I do it. Do you think that's okay? I mean, a lot of people get a little eager when they're brainstorming, right?
Do you find that you frequently make careless mistakes at work or struggle to keep your personal belongings organized?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't say *frequently*, but... I guess I do have a few slip-ups here and there. Nothing dangerous, I promise! 

Just, like... with our paperwork. I'll finish an incident report and hand it in, and I really think it's completely solid, you know? I feel good about it. But then the captain will call me over and point out that I, um... I put the wrong unit number down, or maybe I missed a time stamp. Sometimes I'll just accidentally skip over some little checkbox that actually matters a lot for the safety review. 

I always feel so bad when he has to correct me! I swear I read it over, but my eyes just kind of gloss over those tiny details. I'm usually just trying to get the paperwork filed so I'm ready for the next call. That's just normal clerical stuff, right? I mean, everyone makes a typo or misses a box when they're moving fast... I really hope he knows I take the job seriously. I try my best to be thorough!

Do you find that you have trouble sitting still for long periods, such as when you are at the firehouse or watching a movie, or do you feel a need to fidget or move around when you are expected to stay in one place?

Um... I mean, I can sit still! Mostly. I don't want you to think I'm running around the station when we're supposed to be on standby or anything. 

But, I guess... well, if we're in a long meeting, or even just hanging out in the day room watching TV, I do kind of... keep moving? Like, my leg will start bouncing, or I'll be clicking a pen over and over. Sometimes I'll just keep shifting in my chair or messing with a coaster or whatever is sitting on the table in front of me. 

The thing is, I don't even realize I'm doing it half the time! One of the guys will just reach over and take the pen out of my hand, and I'll be like, "Oh, sorry!" I'm really not trying to be disruptive or annoying, I swear. It just kind of happens when I'm trying to pay attention. That's pretty common, though, right? Like, just a way to burn off some extra energy? I hope the guys don't think I'm too distracting...
